ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What is the approximate molar solubility of zinc iodate at 25°C? Zinc iodate dissociates in water via the following equilibrium process
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows that the dissolution equilibrium of zinc iodate is Zn(IO3)2(s) ⇌ Zn2+(aq) + 2IO3−(aq), and gives Ksp = 4.0 × 10^-6 at 25°C. Let the molar solubility of Zn(IO3)2 be s, then at equilibrium [Zn2+] = s, [IO3−] = 2s. Substitute into the Ksp expression: Ksp = [Zn2+][IO3−]^2 = s(2s)^2 = 4s^3. From 4.0 × 10^-6 = 4s^3, obtain s^3 = 1.0 × 10^-6, so s = 1.0 × 10^-2 M.
